articles.title: RedisInsight exposure can concentrate database credentials
articles.excerpt: RedisInsight exposure can concentrate database credentials RedisInsight is a GUI and command-line client for Redis databases. The Docker service can hold connection definitions, database passwords, an…
articles.body: RedisInsight exposure can concentrate database credentials RedisInsight is a GUI and command-line client for Redis databases. The Docker service can hold connection definitions, database passwords, and workbench history on local storage. That makes an exposed RedisInsight instance more than a convenient dashboard. It may concentrate credentials for several downstream Redis deployments behind one web port. A ZoomEye query for app="RedisInsight" returned 3,203 matches on 28 October 2026, using sub_type=all and a page size of one. A title query returned 5,608. The counts identify candidate services, not confirmed anonymous access or database compromise. A deployment can be intentionally reachable from a trusted administration network and still need tighter controls.
articles.author: SorrelThorncroft

articles.title: Best open-source tools to run multiple AI coding agents in parallel: Orca, herdr and Squadra
articles.excerpt: Once one coding agent is useful, the next step is obvious: run three. One refactors, one writes tests, one chases a bug. Then reality hits. They edit the same files, you lose track of which terminal i…
articles.body: Once one coding agent is useful, the next step is obvious: run three. One refactors, one writes tests, one chases a bug. Then reality hits. They edit the same files, you lose track of which terminal is waiting for an answer, an SSH drop kills an hour of work, and nobody reviews what the agents wrote. A new group of open-source tools fixes exactly this. Three of them cover most needs: Orca : a desktop app that runs several CLI agents side by side, each in its own git worktree. herdr : a terminal runtime that keeps agent sessions alive in the background and tells you which one is blocked. Squadra : a coordination toolkit where Claude Code, Codex and Cursor windows share tasks, and the window that wrote the code never reviews it. Setup commands below come from each README.
articles.author: Deduped

articles.title: Best AI repos for browser automation in 2026: Playwright MCP vs Browser Use vs agent-browser
articles.excerpt: Letting an AI agent use a browser used to mean screenshots, a vision model and a lot of misclicks. That changed. The open-source tools that lead this space in 2026 read the page as structured data (an…
articles.body: Letting an AI agent use a browser used to mean screenshots, a vision model and a lot of misclicks. That changed. The open-source tools that lead this space in 2026 read the page as structured data (an accessibility tree with element references), so the model clicks "@e3" instead of guessing pixel coordinates. There are three repos most people end up choosing between, and they solve different problems: Playwright MCP : Microsoft's MCP server, for when your coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) should drive a real browser. Browser Use : a Python library for building an agent that browses on its own, with any LLM. agent-browser : a fast Rust CLI from Vercel Labs, for agents that work best through short shell commands.

articles.title: Build with AI, Run Without It: Use AI as the Architect, Not the Operator
articles.excerpt: Teams are quietly making AI a runtime dependency. It runs their jobs, triages incidents, fixes bugs and handles daily chores. It works well, until the service is down, the price changes, or the person…
articles.body: Teams are quietly making AI a runtime dependency. It runs their jobs, triages incidents, fixes bugs and handles daily chores. It works well, until the service is down, the price changes, or the person who wrote the prompt leaves and nobody can say what the agent was actually doing. This article argues for a simple alternative: use AI as the architect, not the operator. Use it at build time to produce ordinary, inspectable software, then run that software yourself. Keep AI in the loop only for the genuinely ambiguous remainder. The quiet dependency A pattern has become common. A recurring task, such as reconciling a feed, checking a pipeline or restarting a stuck job, gets handed to an AI agent. It works, so nobody writes or maintains code.

articles.title: The Squash Merge That Broke Our Lullwood Release Train
articles.excerpt: Lullwood, our free browser horror game built in three.js and Next.js, deploys from main, and for a few days in August main quietly stopped sharing history with the branch that feeds it. Nobody told it…
articles.body: Lullwood, our free browser horror game built in three.js and Next.js, deploys from main , and for a few days in August main quietly stopped sharing history with the branch that feeds it. Nobody told it to. This is the git mechanics of how a squash merge did that, and why we found the real cause only on the second try. How the train runs Every feature ships the same way. A branch merges into release/next , and periodically release/next merges into main , which is what actually deploys. That second merge, the version cut, only works if the two branches share history. The automation that merges pull requests was set to squash-merge anything on a branch named lul-* once it carried a ship marker.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 28, 1971: Britain launches its 1st satellite Prospero into space on a Black Arrow rocket
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 28, 1971, the United Kingdom launched its first satellite. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 28, 1971, the United Kingdom launched its first satellite. The satellite was named Prospero, but it was also known as the X-3. This wasn't Britain's first satellite , but it was the first and only one the British space program launched with one of its own rockets. The first six British satellites all launched from the United States on NASA rockets. Prospero launched on a carrier rocket called the Black Arrow. The Prospero mission was the fourth and final flight of a Black Arrow rocket . Prospero was designed to study how the environment in space affects communications satellites. It tested things solar cells and telemetry systems, and even had a micrometeoroid detector that would determine small particles in space posed a threat to the spacecraft.

articles.title: 5 days beneath the waves: What it's like to live in an underwater 'space station'
articles.excerpt: Confined inside a research station 22 feet (7 meters) underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew performed research and maintenance activities like future astronauts on Mars.
articles.body: Living underwater was surprisingly peaceful. It was in many ways exactly what I imagine living on Mars would be like one day. There were no humans around us, except for my three SEA STAR crewmembers and me. Apart from the human noises we made, we couldn't hear anything other than the life support systems keeping us alive submerged 22 feet (7 meters) below the surface. We were living in these extreme conditions to study the challenges astronauts may face on long-duration space missions. Since performing research in space is still rare and expensive, there are numerous facilities around the world that focus on recreating space-like conditions on Earth . One of those stations is the Jules' Undersea Lab, where the SEA STAR simulated space mission took place.

articles.title: ISS astronaut will conduct Canada's 1st spacewalk in 7 years on Oct. 29: Watch it live
articles.excerpt: Joshua Kutryk will venture outside the International Space Station on Oct. 29, on the first spacewalk by a Canadian astronaut in more than seven years. Here's how to watch it live.
articles.body: The next International Space Station (ISS) spacewalk will have more maple-leaf flavor than usual, as a Canadian astronaut will become the first to go outside the orbiting complex in seven years. Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, who's also a colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force, will help the ISS boost its power supply during his first-ever spacewalk on Thursday (Oct. 29). Kutryk will be joined by NASA astronaut Anil Menon, who has done three spacewalks already and also serves as a colonel with the U.S. Space Force . The duo are scheduled to venture outside the orbiting lab at 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT), kicking off a spacewalk that will last roughly 6 hours and 45 minutes. You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 6:30 a.m. EDT (1030 GMT).

articles.title: Meet Apeiron, Virgin Galactic's 1st 'Delta-class' space plane
articles.excerpt: Virgin Galactic has officially unveiled its first "Delta-class" space plane, and announced the results of the worldwide vote to choose its name.
articles.body: Virgin Galactic has officially unveiled the first space plane in its next-gen "Delta" line, and announced the results of the worldwide vote to choose its name. Spaceship Apeiron will be the first Delta-class vehicle, Virgin Galactic revealed on Wednesday (Oct. 28). Apeiron (pronounced "A'-per-on," according to the announcement) takes its name from the ancient Greek word meaning "boundless," and was selected through a public poll that drew votes from thousands of people across 83 countries and six continents. The reveal comes on the same day that the space plane is scheduled to be flown from its manufacturing facility in Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico, where the vehicle will undergo final preparations before beginning flight tests.
